## Details of the Analysis

### Data Preparation and Participant Exclusions

#### Initial Inspection and Grade Availability

The SMARVUS dataset contained 12,570 observations and 788 variables. We checked for identical rows and missing or duplicated participant identifiers ('unique_id'); none were found. Missing reponses were investigated with reference to the variables required for this analysis rather than excluding participants with missing entries in other places of the questionnaire. Statistics attainment was recorded in 'grade', with 1820 participants having a grade entry other than 'NA' or '"Not Available"'.

```{r initial data inspection, include=FALSE}

# Initial dataset inspection
data_summary <- tibble(
  Observations = nrow(smarvus_raw),
  Variables = ncol(smarvus_raw),
  Duplicate_rows = sum(duplicated(smarvus_raw)),
  Duplicate_IDs = sum(duplicated(smarvus_raw$unique_id)),
  Missing_IDs = sum(is.na(smarvus_raw$unique_id))
)

data_summary
```



```{r recorded-grades, include=FALSE}

# Participants with recorded grades
smarvus_grades <- smarvus_raw %>%
  filter(!is.na(grade), grade != "Not Available")

nrow(smarvus_grades)
```

#### Standarising Attainment Across Institutions


Reported grades were recorded differently across the participating surveys. This included different numerical scales, letter grades and ordinal categories. We examined each institutions lowest and highest documented grades before we contrusted a comparable attainment variable. Supported numerical marks (0--100, 0--20, 0--10 and 1--10) were linearly rescaled to a common 0--100 range:

\[
\text{Scaled grade} = 100\,\frac{\text{Observed grade} - \text{Lowest possible grade}}{\text{Highest possible grade} - \text{Lowest possible grade}}.
\]

To keep observations that used letter grades, we usedthe midpoint of the applicable institution-specific percentage band as an *estimated* numerical mark. Grade categories that could not be converted reasonably or defensibly, including the 1--5 ordinal systems, ambiguous entries and values ourside continuous-attainment datasets. This left us with 1362 converted numerical grades and 320 estimated letter grades (1662 observations in total). Grade-band midpoints are approximations, and it is important to note than converting to a common range does not remove the differences in grading standards across different institutions.




```{r grade-systems, include=FALSE}
# Compare grading systems across surveys
grade_summary <- smarvus_grades %>%
  group_by(country, survey_id, grade_low, grade_high) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    Example_grades = paste(head(unique(grade), 3),
                           collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

print(n=22, grade_summary)
```

```{r grade-boundaries, include=FALSE}
# Institution-specific letter grade boundaries

grade_boundaries <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    survey_id = "brawijaya",
    grade = c("A", "B+", "B", "C+", "C", "D+", "D", "E"),
    lower = c(80, 75, 69, 60, 55, 50, 44, 0),
    upper = c(100, 80, 75, 69, 60, 55, 50, 44)
  ),

  tibble(
    survey_id = "york_can",
    grade = c("A+", "A", "B+", "B", "C+", "C", "D+", "D", "E", "F"),
    lower = c(90, 80, 75, 70, 65, 60, 55, 50, 40, 0),
    upper = c(100, 89, 79, 74, 69, 64, 59, 54, 49, 39)
  ),

  tibble(
    survey_id = "mef",
    grade = c("A", "A-", "B+", "B", "B-", "C+", "C", "C-", "D+", "D", "F"),
    lower = c(90, 80, 75, 70, 65, 60, 55, 50, 45, 35, 0),
    upper = c(100, 89, 79, 74, 69, 64, 59, 54, 49, 44, 35)
  ),

  tibble(
    survey_id = "limerick",
    grade = c("A1", "A2", "B1", "B2", "B3", "C1", "C2", "C3", "D1", "D2", "F"),
    lower = c(80, 75, 70, 65, 60, 55, 50, 45, 40, 35, 0),
    upper = c(100, 79, 74, 69, 64, 59, 54, 49, 44, 39, 35)
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    grade_midpoint = (lower + upper) / 2
  )

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(grade_boundaries[c("survey_id", "grade")]))


```



```{r prepare-grades, include=FALSE}
# Prepare numerical grades
smarvus_prepared <- smarvus_raw %>%
  mutate(
    
    grade_clean = str_trim(grade),
    
    # Convert numbers stored as text
    grade_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(str_remove(grade_clean, "%$"))),
    grade_low_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(grade_low)),
    grade_high_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(grade_high)),

    # Identify supported numerical grading systems
    supported_numeric =
      (grade_low_num == 0 & grade_high_num %in% c(10, 20, 100)) |
      (grade_low_num == 1 & grade_high_num == 10),

    # Check that marks are within their grading range
    valid_numeric =
      supported_numeric &
      !is.na(grade_num) &
      grade_num >= grade_low_num &
      grade_num <= grade_high_num) %>%

  # Add letter-grade midpoint conversions
  left_join(
    grade_boundaries %>%
      select(survey_id, grade, grade_midpoint),
    by = c("survey_id", "grade_clean" = "grade")) %>%

  # Create a single attainment variable
  mutate(
    grade_scaled = coalesce(
      if_else(valid_numeric,
        100 * (grade_num - grade_low_num) / (grade_high_num - grade_low_num),
        NA_real_),
      grade_midpoint),

    grade_method = case_when(
      !is.na(grade_midpoint) ~ "Letter grade midpoint",
      !is.na(grade_scaled) ~ "Numerical conversion",
      TRUE ~ "Unresolved or unavailable"))

# Check conversion results
smarvus_prepared %>%
  filter(!is.na(grade_clean), grade_clean != "Not Available") %>%
  count(grade_method)
```

```{r unresolved-grades, include=FALSE}
# Inspect observations without a usable converted grade
smarvus_prepared %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(grade_clean),
    grade_clean != "Not Available",
    is.na(grade_scaled)
  ) %>%
  
  count(survey_id, grade_clean, sort = TRUE)
```

#### Attention Checks and Exclusion Criteria


We assessed response quality using the six attention check items and the 'attention_amnesty' response. Participants were excluded if they answered at least one administered check incorrectly or explicitly selected '"No"' to the amnesty question. Missing check or amnesty responses were **not** interpreted as failures as the questions were not necessarily recorded for every survey. Under these rules, 1542 participants remained after attainment and quality screening. This is the *data-preparation sample*, not necessarily the final analysis sample: the anxiety-scale completeness criteria will be applied subsequently.

```{r attention-checks, include=FALSE}
# Attention check variables
check_cols <- c(
  "Q7.1_24",
  "Q8.1_21",
  "Q9.1_22",
  "Q11.1_9",
  "Q13.1_17",
  "Q15.1_9"
)

# Count checks answered
smarvus_prepared$n_checks_answered <-
  rowSums(!is.na(smarvus_prepared[, check_cols]))

# Count incorrect responses to answered checks
smarvus_prepared <- smarvus_prepared %>%
  mutate(
    n_checks_failed =
      as.integer(!is.na(Q7.1_24) & Q7.1_24 != 1) +
      as.integer(!is.na(Q8.1_21) & Q8.1_21 != 5) +
      as.integer(!is.na(Q9.1_22) & Q9.1_22 != 1) +
      as.integer(!is.na(Q11.1_9) & Q11.1_9 != 3) +
      as.integer(!is.na(Q13.1_17) & Q13.1_17 != 2) +
      as.integer(!is.na(Q15.1_9) & Q15.1_9 != 4)
  )

# Summarise attention check results for usable grades
smarvus_prepared %>%
  filter(!is.na(grade_scaled)) %>%
  count(n_checks_answered, n_checks_failed)

```

```{r participant-exclusions, include=FALSE}
# Participants with usable attainment
valid_grades <- smarvus_prepared %>%
  filter(!is.na(grade_scaled))

# Exclude explicit amnesty refusals
amnesty_passed <- valid_grades %>%
  filter(
    is.na(attention_amnesty) |
      attention_amnesty != "No")

# Exclude incorrect answered attention checks
smarvus_clean <- amnesty_passed %>%
  filter(n_checks_failed == 0)
```

The participant counts at each stage are summarised in the table below. Of the 1542 kept observations, 165 had no recorded attention check answers and 70 had a missing amnesty response. So, the conclusions should be checked for the sensitivity to the treatment of missing quality information. Results could also depend on if the estimated letter grades are included.

```{r exclusion-table, echo=FALSE}
exclusion_flow <- tibble(
  Stage = c(
    "Original dataset",
    "Non-missing grade entries",
    "Usable standardised attainment",
    "After attention amnesty",
    "After attention checks"
  ),

  N = c(
    nrow(smarvus_raw),
    nrow(smarvus_grades),
    nrow(valid_grades),
    nrow(amnesty_passed),
    nrow(smarvus_clean)
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    Excluded = lag(N) - N
  )

knitr::kable(exclusion_flow)
```

```{r validation-export, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(smarvus_clean$grade_scaled),
  all(is.finite(smarvus_clean$grade_scaled)),
  all(smarvus_clean$grade_scaled >= 0),
  all(smarvus_clean$grade_scaled <= 100),
  all(smarvus_clean$n_checks_failed == 0),
  n_distinct(smarvus_clean$unique_id) == nrow(smarvus_clean)
)

write_csv(smarvus_clean, "smarvus_clean.csv")
write_csv(exclusion_flow, "exclusion_flow.csv")
```

RMARS is revised mathematics anxiety rating scale (NORMAL MATHS ANXIETY ONE) Q8.2_1 to Q8.2_24
RMARS-S is like RMARS but replaces the maths with stats Q7.2_1 to Q7.2_23
STARS is statistics anxiety rating scale (NORMAL STATS ANXIETY ONE) Q7.1_1 to Q7.1_23
STARS-M is a modified version of STARS but replaces the stats with maths Q8.1_1 to Q8.1_20
